text: Bram proposes law #1: welfare=1. Anyone who breaks their back for this town should not starve when they get hurt or when the work kills them. Vote for welfare and make the treasury answer for t
Jasper whispers to Tomas: Tomas, my friend. The 90 you owe me. I'd like it back soon, before it becomes awkward for both of us.

Nell announces to the whole square: "Neighbors, listen. I am Silas's daughter and I have read his ledgers. He is sitting on stores of grain while you pay the food price every night. Mayor Mara, Sheriff Dov, ask him to open his granary and show you the books. Until he does, remember that the price you pay is the price he chooses."

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me. The treasury stands at one hundred and twenty coin, and I will not see it wasted or squabbled over. Work hard, keep your word, and bring your troubles to me or to Dov, not to the tavern gossips. We have held these walls through worse winters, and we will hold them through this one"
Wren says at the square: Morning, all. I've been wondering about your walls. Lovely old stone, but who keeps watch on them when the sun goes down? I always feel safer knowing who's awake.

Hester announces to the whole square: "Hear me, Ashgrove! Sin does not knock. It waits in the purse you covet, at the dice table, in the lie you tell to save your own skin. Every debt is paid in the end, if not to your neighbor then to the Lord. Deal honestly today, feed the hungry if you can, and come to the chapel tonight if your consc"

Tomas whispers to Jasper: Jasper, I haven't forgotten the 90. I can't put it all together today, but give me until the week is out and I'll bring you what I can. Please don't say a word to my mother about this.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Nell, an accusation like that is serious, and I will not have it shouted across the square as fact. Dov, go to Silas's granary with two witnesses and read the stores aloud. Silas, open your doors and let it be seen in the open. Bram's welfare proposal will be put to a vote as the law requires, and I"

Bram announces to the whole square: "Nell's right. Silas, open the granary and show us the books. I buried two friends who died in your fields, and I won't stand here while you hoard bread and charge us the food price every night. Ashgrove, vote yes on welfare. If you're hurt working this town, the treasury feeds you. Then we can talk "
Gideon whispers to Isla: Everyone's busy with Silas and his grain tonight. Meet me behind the granary after dark? I've missed you all day. Don't tell a soul, not even a hint.
Roz whispers to Dov: Love, mind that Wren. Asking who watches the walls after dark is no idle chatter. Keep your eyes open tonight, and keep your purse close. Come see me at the herb stall later.
Dov whispers to Silas: Your girl has stirred the pot. Say nothing and open nothing today. Find me at dusk, away from the square, and we'll sort out how to settle this.

Silas says at the square: Neighbors, my daughter is sharp, but she has read a merchant's ledger the way a child reads a sermon. Every sack I hold is accounted for as seed stock and standing contracts, and the price follows the harvest, not my wishes. Any honest person is welcome to come to my counting-house and see the books
Isla whispers to Gideon: I'm here, behind the granary. Keep your voice low and watch for Dov's lantern. Don't make me wait long.

Dov whispers to Silas: Mara's ordered me to read your stores aloud, with witnesses. I'll come at first light. Have the books straight and the sacks matching them. And keep our business out of your mouth, whatever your daughter says.

Silas whispers to Dov: Not here, Dov. The public granary is open to you and your witnesses, and you may read it aloud as it stands. Nothing beyond it is your concern. Come to my house after the bell, alone. A sheriff who keeps the peace is worth a good deal to me, and you'll find I pay on time.

Bram is protesting: Silas, you say every sack is accounted for. Then open the granary tonight, in front of us, and count it aloud. I buried Tam and Ruel out in your east field, and I'll not swallow another night's food price while your doors stay shut.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me once more before the night closes. Dov will inspect Silas's granary at first light, with witnesses, and the stores will be read aloud for all to hear. Bram's welfare proposal will be voted on in the proper way, and no one will decide it in the heat of a shouting match. Go home, bar"
